key_insight: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting (CoPE) improves language-agent training by adding multi-step action prediction as supervision, so the same policy backbone learns to act and forecast from intermediate histories instead of only terminal rewards.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for building more sample-efficient agentic RL systems that reduce costly long-horizon rollouts while keeping inference unchanged and lightweight.
method: Train on successful on-policy trajectories using multi-step action targets derived from future action sequences.
Also supervise the policy by forecasting actions from preceding histories, creating a temporal ensemble of signals.
Use a single shared policy backbone, so acting and forecasting co-evolve without extra models or inference overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, τ²-bench, and AppWorld) with stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and other RL baselines, including up to 1.9× and 2.0× higher sample efficiency on ScienceWorld.
watch_item: The approach depends on successful on-policy trajectories for constructing action targets, so performance may be sensitive to trajectory quality and rollout stability during training.
paper_title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
